posts.content:
Only 11% of banks say they've actually cracked trustworthy AI at scale. Most are still stuck circling the pilot stage.

Piergiorgio Grossi has a theory on why — and it doesn't start with technology. Before joining Credem as Chief Innovation & Data Officer, he spent over a decade in Formula 1 at Ferrari, before digital transformation at Ducati. 

🎧 In this episode of Pragmatism in Practice he tells something every leader chasing "AI transformation" should sit with: "I've never seen a problem solved just because you bought a piece of software."

A few ideas from the conversation that stuck with us:

🔷 Explore and exploit aren't two sequential phases — they're a continuous loop. Treating them as a one-way handoff is a big part of why so many AI pilots never convert to value.

🔷 Every organization has a "heartbeat" — the natural rhythm at which decisions need revisiting. In Formula 1, it's every race. In banking, most leaders have never actually defined theirs.

🔷 Innovation only scales when failure has an owner. Piergiorgio's rule at Credem: "If we fail, it's my fault... I have a salary because I fail."

Hear the full conversation with Piergiorgio Grossi on Pragmatism in Practice, here👇

https://bit.ly/468jZnR

#AgenticAI #BFSI #Banking

Most AI discussions focus purely on the technology. But as organizations move beyond experimentation, the real differentiator will be delivery excellence. Based on platform modernization programs, successful AI delivery depends on five pillars:

📈 Value: Measuring success by business outcomes, not technical milestones.

posts.content:
AI unit costs have dropped 90% since 2023. So why are enterprise AI bills skyrocketing?
 
As organizations scale from simple prompts to complex agentic workflows, token consumption is exploding. But asking teams to write 'tidier prompts' won't fix the problem. Managing AI spend is an architecture challenge, not a user habit problem.

Speaking with Aaron Tan for ComputerWeekly.com, our Chief Data & AI Officer Shayan Mohanty breaks down how to master AI operating economics:
 
- Shift infrastructure: Rent dedicated GPUs and leverage open-weight models for predictable costs.
- Fix agentic traps: Solve backend architectural bottlenecks like the 'stampeding herd' caching problem.
- Focus on ROI: Move from tracking raw token spend to measuring true business profitability.
 
"There are no tech moats anymore, the only thing that matters is execution moats and adapting faster than everyone else." — Shayan Mohanty

Read the full analysis: https://lnkd.in/dRcWxrmU

Five years ago, Elizabeth Parra joined Thoughtworks as a marketing intern, starting a new chapter in her career in the middle of a very unusual time.

It was 2021, her first experience with a global company and, as Elizabeth openly admits, she was still figuring out exactly what Thoughtworks did. So she got curious.

During her first few months, Elizabeth listened to Thoughtworks podcasts in Spanish to learn more about the company and how we work. She became interested in how agile practices showed up in everyday work and found herself learning alongside people from different teams and parts of the world.

Over the next four years, Elizabeth built a career shaped by experiences she never expected to have, people she learned from and a culture she came to value even more with time.

Eventually, her career took her in a different direction and, after exploring another industry, back to tech.

Recently, Elizabeth reconnected with Thoughtworks at an alumni event, giving her a chance to reflect on what had stayed with her since leaving.

"When you move on and don't find that same environment elsewhere, you realize how much you miss it."

For Elizabeth, that includes the people, the way they supported one another and an experience that helped shape the professional she is today.
